transcript.content: Hello, welcome to the clinic. What brings you in to see us today?

I can’t shake this feeling that I’m a terrible person and that everything that’s gone wrong is my fault, like I’ve already messed up my whole life. I just feel so heavy and guilty all the time, and my aunt and pastor insisted that I come here to talk to someone.
How long have you been feeling this overwhelming sense of guilt and heaviness, was it triggered by a specific event or has it been building up over time?

This heavy feeling has been building up for a little over a year, starting when I was pushing myself so hard to finish my GED and CNA classes while working extra shifts. As I fell behind in school and made mistakes at work, the stress just piled up, and now I feel like I've completely let down my mom, my church, and God.
Have you experienced any periods in the past year where you felt significantly better for a few weeks or more, or has this heavy feeling and guilt been constant since it started?

No, it’s been pretty much constant this whole year without any real breaks. At most, I’ll have a rare day where the heavy cloud lifts just a little, and the voice and those awful thoughts of being cursed will quiet down, but it never lasts more than a day before it all comes back.

Have you had any episodes of feeling significantly better for at least two months at any point in your life before this past year, or has this constant feeling of guilt and heaviness been a persistent issue with no prolonged periods of relief?

Before this past year, I was actually doing completely fine and didn't feel this way at all. I used to really enjoy going to Zumba, hiking on the weekends, and being active at my church without any of this heaviness or guilt. But since all of this started about fourteen months ago, it's just been a constant struggle with no real relief.

Have you experienced more than one episode of feeling significantly better for at least two months before this current period of constant guilt and heaviness, or was this the first time you've struggled with these feelings for an extended period?

No, this is the first time I've ever gone through anything like this. Before I started pushing myself so hard with the GED and extra shifts about fourteen months ago, I was doing okay and keeping up with my church and Zumba. This past year has just been one long, continuous struggle without any breaks.

You mentioned this is the first time you've experienced such a long period of guilt and heaviness, but can you tell me if you've had any previous episodes of feeling down or depressed that lasted for more than two weeks but less than two months before this current episode started?

I don't recall ever having a period of feeling down or depressed like this before this past year. I was usually busy but generally doing okay and staying active with my routines. This is definitely the first time I've ever struggled with these kinds of feelings.

You've mentioned this is your first episode of feeling this way, but to clarify, have you had any periods of at least two weeks where you felt relatively normal or even happy since this constant feeling of guilt and heaviness started about fourteen months ago?

No, I haven't had even two weeks of feeling normal or happy since this all started. It has just been one continuous dark period for over a year now. At most, I might get a single day where the heaviness lifts a tiny bit and the voice quiets down, but I never get a real break.

You've had this constant feeling of guilt and heaviness for over a year without any significant breaks, but can you tell me if you've experienced any changes in the intensity of these feelings over time, or have they remained relatively consistent?

For the most part, the heavy, dark feeling has stayed really consistent and exhausting every single day. There are only very rare days when it lifts just a tiny bit, and on those days, the negative voices quiet down and the feeling of being cursed doesn't feel quite as strong. Otherwise, it has just been a continuous, heavy struggle that doesn't really change.
Have you experienced significant changes in your sleep or appetite patterns since this constant feeling of guilt and heaviness started about fourteen months ago?

My sleep has been absolutely terrible; I lie awake for hours replaying all my mistakes, and when I finally drift off, I wake up at 3 or 4 AM with my heart racing and can't get back to sleep. As for my appetite, I don't even have the energy to cook anymore, so my aunt has to bring me food, which just leaves me feeling completely exhausted and drained.
You mentioned enjoying activities like Zumba and hiking before this period started, but have you found any pleasure or interest in these or other activities since the heavy feeling and guilt began?

No, I don't find any pleasure in them anymore. Things I used to love, like Zumba or helping at the youth center, just feel completely pointless and far away now. It's like I'm watching my life from under water.

You've described this as your first episode of feeling this way, lasting over a year without significant relief, but can you confirm if you've had any shorter periods of feeling down or depressed before this that might have lasted less than two weeks?
No, I don't recall having any short periods of feeling down or depressed like this before this past year started. I was always pretty active and doing okay back then.
To confirm, you're saying that this is your first episode of depression, and it has lasted for more than two weeks, correct?

Yes, that's correct. This is the first time I've ever felt like this, and it has been going on for a little over a year now, not just a couple of weeks. It all started back when I began pushing myself so hard with my GED and the extra work shifts.

You mentioned you no longer find pleasure in activities like Zumba or helping at the youth center, but have you completely lost interest in all activities you once enjoyed, or are there any that still bring you some small amount of joy or satisfaction?

Yes, I have completely lost interest in everything, and absolutely nothing brings me joy anymore. Even the things I used to love just feel pointless and so far away now. It really feels like I'm just watching my life happen from underwater.
Can you tell me if there was a specific point or event when your feelings of guilt and heaviness started to become constant, or was it a gradual process over several months?

It was definitely a gradual process that built up over about fourteen months. It started when I began pushing myself really hard to finish my GED while juggling all those extra work shifts, and it just slowly got worse over time. As I lost my routines and fell behind in school, the heaviness and guilt just kept growing until it became constant.
Have you ever had thoughts of harming yourself or wished you were dead since this heavy feeling and guilt started?

Yes, almost every day I catch myself thinking it would be better if I just didn’t wake up, since I feel like such a burden to everyone. On my worst nights, I've sat on my bed holding my old pain pills, planning out how many it would take to finally end things.

You've described a continuous period of guilt and heaviness for over a year without significant relief, but can you clarify if there have been any fluctuations in the severity of your symptoms during this time, such as periods where the feelings of guilt were slightly less intense?

There are very rare days when the dark cloud lifts just a little bit and the heavy guilt isn't quite as strong. On those days, the feeling that God has cursed me fades slightly and the voice in my ear quiets down. But it never lasts more than a day before it all comes right back.
Have you ever acted on those thoughts of harming yourself or have a specific plan in place to end your life, or are they just recurring thoughts?

I haven't actually taken them, but I still think about wishing I wouldn't wake up almost every single day. On my worst nights, I've sat on my bed holding my old pain pills, planning out how many it would take to end my life so I won't be a burden anymore. I feel so deeply ashamed to admit that, but I haven't gone through with it.
Have you ever told anyone else about these thoughts of wishing you wouldn't wake up or your plans with the pain pills, or is this something you've kept to yourself?
No, I haven't really shared those specific thoughts or the plan with the pills with anyone else. I've kept them mostly to myself because I'm just too ashamed of it all.
You've mentioned a voice in your ear and feelings of being cursed; can you tell me more about these experiences, such as what the voice says or when you hear it?

It's so hard to talk about, but when I'm alone late at night, I hear a man's voice right behind my left ear telling me I'm worthless, that I've disappointed God, and that something terrible will happen to my family because of me. I also truly believe that because of my mistakes with my GED and at work, God has marked me as cursed. It feels like everyone around me can see it on me and is just waiting for me to fail again.

Can you describe in more detail when and how you hear this voice, and if there are any other unusual experiences, like seeing things that aren't there, that you've had since this heavy feeling started?

The voice is a man's voice that sounds like it's whispering right behind my left ear, usually late at night when I'm alone after a shift. It tells me I'm worthless, that I've disappointed God, and that something terrible is going to happen to my family. I don't see anything that isn't there, but hearing him is so incredibly real and terrifying.
Have you experienced any other unusual perceptions, such as seeing or smelling things that others can't, in addition to hearing the voice?
No, I don't see or smell anything unusual that isn't really there. The experience is completely limited to hearing that man's voice whispering behind my left ear when I'm alone.
Can you tell me more about what you mean by 'God has marked me as cursed' and if you believe this is a fact or just a feeling you have?

I know it sounds crazy to others, but I am deeply convinced it's a fact that God has cursed me because of my failures with school and work. It feels like an undeniable reality, and I truly believe everyone can see it on me and is just waiting for me to fail. On the rare days when my depression lifts slightly, the thought fades, but when I'm really low, it feels entirely like a fact.
Have you experienced any other hallucinations, such as seeing things that aren't there, in addition to hearing the voice behind your left ear?
No, I have never seen things that aren't there. It is strictly just hearing that man's voice whispering right behind my left ear when I'm by myself.
Can you confirm if the voice you hear and the feeling of being cursed are present all the time, or do they come and go?

They aren't constant; they are really tied to how low I'm feeling. On the rare days when the heavy cloud lifts a little, the voice quiets down and the feeling of being cursed fades away. But as soon as my mood drops low again, they both come back just as strong.
Have you ever had any periods where the voice behind your ear stopped completely for more than a few days, or has it been consistently present whenever you're feeling low?

No, it has never stopped for more than a day because I haven't had a real break from this depression. The voice only started after this dark period began about a year ago, and it never happened to me before that. It is completely tied to my mood, so it only quiets down on those rare days when the heaviness lifts a little.
Can you describe if the voice you hear ever tells you to do things or gives you commands, rather than just criticizing you or making statements?

No, the voice never gives me commands or tells me to do anything. It only criticizes me and makes statements, telling me that I'm worthless, that I've disappointed God, and warning me that something bad is going to happen to my family because of me.
Have you ever experienced any other types of hallucinations, such as feeling things on your skin or tasting things that aren't there, in addition to hearing the voice?

No, I've never experienced anything like feeling things on my skin or tasting things that aren't there. The only thing I experience is hearing that man's voice whispering behind my left ear late at night when I'm all alone.
Can you confirm if the voice you hear is always critical and never supportive or encouraging, and if it has ever commented on your thoughts or actions in a way that feels like it's reading your mind?

Yes, it is always deeply critical and negative, never supportive, and constantly tells me that I'm worthless and have disappointed God. It doesn't literally read my mind, but it feels like it knows exactly what I'm feeling because it always brings up my deepest failures and my fears about something bad happening to my family.
Have you ever felt like the voice you hear is a part of your own thoughts, or is it always experienced as coming from outside of yourself?

No, it doesn't feel like my own thoughts at all; it is definitely experienced as coming from outside of myself. It sounds like a distinct man's voice speaking right behind my left ear, even though I know there is actually no one there in the room when it happens.
Can you tell me more about when the voice behind your ear first started, and if it coincided with the beginning of your feelings of guilt and heaviness, or if it started at a different time?

The voice only started after I began feeling really overwhelmed, guilty, and depressed about a year ago when I fell behind with my GED and work. I had never heard any voices before this dark period began, and on the rare days when my heavy mood lifts a little, the voice quiets down as well.
